topic: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL ships NVFP4-only and what that means for local hardware
hook_candidates: Seventy-five gigabytes your GPU cannot read.
NVIDIA's new four-bit file skips your GPU.
Your GPU isn't too small. It's too old.
Check one number before you download Nemotron.
The most downloaded Nemotron won't run here.
Blackwell only: NVIDIA shipped a format gate.
Can your card do four-bit math?
title: Nemotron NVFP4: your GPU might be too old
description: NVIDIA posted Nemotron 3.5 Super VL as an NVFP4 checkpoint, and that format only accelerates on Blackwell. You will learn which file your GPU can actually run: the NVFP4 original or a GGUF re-quant. Full guide on the channel page. (Narration is AI-generated.)

scenes.narration: You downloaded the wrong Nemotron. The seventy-five gigabyte file everyone grabbed may not run on your card.
scenes.on_screen_text: You downloaded the wrong Nemotron. | 75 GB NVFP4
scenes.visual_brief: Frame 1: dark canvas, hook line 'You downloaded the wrong Nemotron.' centered in the upper third, fully legible. At 0.35 s a file card labeled 'NVFP4' rises in place at center; on 'seventy-five gigabyte file' a giant amber '75 GB' scales in on the card. On 'may not run on your card' the card's amber edge dims to gray and a hairline crack fades across it. Only the card and number animate; entrances are rise-in-place or scale; everything sits above the caption band.

scenes.narration: Inside, weights are quantized, stored in fewer bits, four each. Sixteen weights share a scale, which shrinks the file.
scenes.on_screen_text: 4 bits per weight | 16 weights share a scale
scenes.visual_brief: Sixteen small square cells fade in as a row under 'weights are quantized'; on 'four each' each cell is stamped '4 bits'. On 'Sixteen weights share a scale' the stamps fade out, the cells cluster into one amber-outlined block, and a single chip labeled 'a scale' fades in above it. On 'which shrinks the file' the whole block scales down into a small file glyph at center. Dark background, amber #FFB347 accents, one text block animating at a time, content above the caption band.
scenes.render_notes: Manim: 16-cell VGroup with 0.06 s staggered fade-ins; stamps as small Text children; final scale-down about 0.4 s.

scenes.narration: Four-bit math at speed needs Blackwell tensor cores. Compute capability, your GPU's feature version, must read ten point zero. The blocker is generation, not size.
scenes.visual_brief: On 'needs Blackwell tensor cores' two GPU slabs fade in side by side: left labeled 'Blackwell' with lit amber traces, right dim gray labeled 'older'. On 'must read ten point zero' a badge '10.0' scales in over the Blackwell slab. On 'The blocker is generation, not size' a vertical amber gate line rises in place between the slabs and the gray slab dims further. Small labels '4-bit math' and 'compute capability' fade in one at a time above the slabs. Fade and scale entrances only; nothing in the bottom 450 px.
scenes.render_notes: Hyperframes: keep the 10.0 badge scale-in under 0.3 s; the gate line rises only after the badge settles.

scenes.narration: Below that version, grab a GGUF re-quant, the format llama.cpp tools load, rebuilt from the reference weights. The re-quant is a power adapter, except this one rebuilds the appliance.
scenes.visual_brief: The gate line fades as a horizontal ladder base fades in on 'Below that version'. On 'grab a GGUF re-quant' three rung cards rise in place, the first labeled 'GGUF re-quant'. On 'rebuilt from the reference weights' a tall dim slab labeled 'reference weights' fades in behind the ladder, thin lines feeding each rung. On 'forty-six point one gigabytes' the first rung lights amber with the text 'starts at 46.1 GB'; upper rungs stay gray and unlabeled. Rise-in-place only, at most two elements moving at once.

scenes.narration: Unsloth's re-quant ladder starts at forty-six point one gigabytes of download.
scenes.visual_brief: Giant amber '46.1 GB' types on over the dark slab as the narration says 'forty-six point one'; a thin capacity bar fills beneath it to the 'gigabytes of download' phrase, comparing against a ghosted 75 GB outline behind. No edge motion; the number scales up 1.05 in place after the bar fills.

scenes.narration: Check your card's compute capability: ten point zero takes the file, older takes the re-quant. Not a file size, a hardware commitment.

scenes.visual_brief: On 'A re-quant is different weights' the line 'different weights, not unpacked' fades in at center, then fades out on 'Check your card's compute capability' as two stacked cards fade in: the frame-1 NVFP4 file card returns on top tagged '10.0' with a small check for 'ten point zero takes the file', and a 'GGUF' card tagged 'older' fades in below for 'older takes the re-quant', both with the same amber edge. Final frame holds the two centered cards, a rhyme of frame 1's single card, while the wordmark settles in the last half second.

narration_full: You downloaded the wrong Nemotron. The seventy-five gigabyte file everyone grabbed may not run on your card. Inside, weights are quantized, stored in fewer bits, four each. Sixteen weights share a scale, which shrinks the file. Four-bit math at speed needs Blackwell tensor cores. Compute capability, your GPU's feature version, must read ten point zero. The blocker is generation, not size. Below that version, grab a GGUF re-quant, the format llama.cpp tools load, rebuilt from the reference weights. The re-quant is a power adapter, except this one rebuilds the appliance. Unsloth's re-quant ladder starts at forty-six point one gigabytes of download. Check your card's compute capability: ten point zero takes the file, older takes the re-quant. Not a file size, a hardware commitment.
